system_name: Prefrontal cortex bump-attractor working memory circuit
description: Stimulus-selective persistent activity in dlPFC arises from a cortical microcircuit in which pyramidal neurons with similar preferred directions excite one another via NMDA-dominated recurrent synapses, while PV+ basket cells provide broad, relatively unstructured feedback inhibition. The resulting effective Mexican-hat connectivity supports a continuous (bump) attractor on a ring of tuned neurons that maintains a spatial cue across the delay period. Slow NMDA kinetics stabilize the bump against synchronous instabilities, and the broad inhibition confers distractor resistance, reproducing Funahashi/Goldman-Rakic delay-cell properties.
